svg.text: 494 nodes · 392 relationships · 529 implied labels, generated from the DEXPI specification 2.0.1 model sources (GitLab dexpi/Specification, tag V2.0.1). The main arrows are named by their relationship type; hover any arrow for its name and description, and cards link to the specification page.
Core — data types, quantities and diagrams
Plant — structure, equipment, piping and instrumentation
subtype: also carries the supertype's label

path.title: HAS_CONCEPTUAL_MODEL: The conceptual model of the EngineeringModel. Each EngineeringModel has at most one ConceptualModel. A composition: each ConceptualModel is part of at most one owner and is deleted with it.
HAS_DIAGRAM: The diagram of the EngineeringModel. Each EngineeringModel has at most one Diagram. A composition: each Diagram is part of at most one owner and is deleted with it.

RotaryMixer — A Mixer machine that mixes by means of rotating components. Properties: id, upperLimitAllowableDesignPressureDrop, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower

Kneader — A machine that is capable of mixing and working into a uniform mass by, or as if by, folding, pressing, and stretching. Properties: id, upperLimitAllowableDesignPressureDrop, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
Pump — A machine that is capable of pumping but may require parts and subsystems for that capability. Properties: id, designPressureHead, designVolumeFlowRate, differentialPressure
CentrifugalPump — Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
RotaryPump — Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
ReciprocatingPump — Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
EjectorPump — Properties: id, designCapacityMotiveFluid
Compressor — A machine that has the capability of compressing a gas. Properties: id, designVolumeFlowRate, differentialPressure
AirEjector — Properties: id, designCapacityMotiveFluid

AxialCompressor — A Compressor in which the gas is accelerated by the action of a bladed rotor and where the main flow is along the rotation axis of the rotor. Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
CentrifugalCompressor — Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
ReciprocatingCompressor — Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
RotaryCompressor — Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
StationaryTransportSystem — A transport system that is intended to transport, store or load/unload material and that, as a whole, remains in one place. Properties: id, designPower
Conveyor — A machine that is capable of conveying material. Properties: id, conveyorType, conveyingDistance, designCapacityMassFlowRate, designRotationalSpeed

Lift — A StationaryTransportSystem for transporting persons or things from one level to another (from <http://data.posccaesar.org/rdl/RDS13601120>_). Properties: id, dischargeHead, upperLimitLoadCapacity, upperLimitVolumeCapacity
LoadingUnloadingSystem — Properties: id, upperLimitConveyingDistance, upperLimitDischargeHead, upperLimitLoadCapacity
MobileTransportSystem — A mobile system that is intended to transport, store or load/unload material. Properties: id, upperLimitLoadCapacity, upperLimitVolumeCapacity

ForkliftTruck — A MobileTransportSystem and vehicle with power operated prongs that can be raised and lowered by will, for loading, transporting and unloading goods (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS11590075>_). Properties: id, upperLimitDischargeHead
RailWaggon — A non self driving vehicle and mobile transport system intended to ride on rails. Properties: id
Ship — A watercraft and MobileTransportSystem that is a sea-going vessel of considerable size. Properties: id
TransportableContainer — Properties: id
Truck — Properties: id

PackagingSystem — A system that is intended for the preparation of goods for transport, warehousing, logistics, sale, and end use (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS2228725>_). Properties: id, designCapacityPackagingUnits, packagingSystemType, designCapacityMassFlowRate, designPower

Feeder — A closed fluid transporter that is a gathering line tied into a trunk line (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS300644>_). Properties: id, upperLimitDesignParticleSize, designMassFlowRate, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
SprayNozzle — Properties: id, designVolumeFlowRate, subTagName
Blower — Properties: id, designDifferentialPressure, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower, designVolumeFlowRate
Fan — Properties: id, designDifferentialPressure, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower, designVolumeFlowRate
AxialBlower — Properties: id
CentrifugalBlower — A blower in which one ore more impellers accelerate the flow and where the main flow through the impeller is radial. Properties: id
AxialFan — Properties: id
RadialFan — Properties: id
Screw — Properties: id, diameter, materialOfConstructionCode, stageIdentifier
Extruder — A machine that has the capability of extruding (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS394044551>_). Properties: id, designMassFlowRate, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
RotatingExtruder — Properties: id
ReciprocatingExtruder — Properties: id

Agglomerator — A machine that is capable of agglomerating. It is usually vertically aligned. Properties: id, designLiquidFeedMassFlowRate, designSolidFeedMassFlowRate, designMassFlowRate, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower, designVolumeFlowRate
BriquettingRoller — An element of an Agglomerator that compresses bulk material into briquettes. Properties: id, diameter, materialOfConstructionCode, stageIdentifier
RotatingPressureAgglomerator — An Agglomerator which uses briquetting rollers to produce pressure and to form material. Properties: id, lowerLimitDesignPressingForce, upperLimitDesignPressingForce

ReciprocatingPressureAgglomerator — An Agglomerator which uses pistons to produce pressure and to form material (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS2228720>_). Properties: id, lowerLimitDesignPressingForce, upperLimitDesignPressingForce
PelletizerDisc — A rotating disc as a component of an Agglomerator. Properties: id, diameter, materialOfConstructionCode
RotatingGrowthAgglomerator — An Agglomerator which uses a pelletizer disc to produce pellets. Properties: id
Mill — Properties: id, lowerLimitDesignOutputParticleSize, upperLimitDesignInputParticleSize, upperLimitDesignOutputParticleSize, designCapacityMassFlowRate, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
Crusher — Properties: id
CrusherElement — A functional component of a Crusher. Properties: id, crusherElementType, materialOfConstructionCode, stageIdentifier
Grinder — A Mill that has the capability of grinding. Properties: id
GrindingElement — A functional component of a Grinder. Properties: id, grindingElementType, materialOfConstructionCode, stageIdentifier
Centrifuge — Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower, designVolumeFlowRate
FilteringCentrifugeDrum — A drum being a component of a FilteringCentrifuge. Properties: id, diameter, materialOfConstructionCode
FilteringCentrifuge — A centrifuge intended to separate solids from liquids by centrifugal process based on particle size. Properties: id, minimumParticleSize
SedimentalCentrifuge — A centrifuge that is intended to separate solids from liquids by a centrifugal process based on different densities. Properties: id, efficiency
SedimentalCentrifugeDrum — A SedimentalCentrifugeDrum is a drum and a component of a SedimentalCentrifuge. Properties: id, diameter, materialOfConstructionCode

DryingChamber — A device that is a chamber, fixed or portable, for drying used as a component of an apparatus or a machine. Properties: id, designVolumeFlowRate, materialOfConstructionCode, subTagName

Dryer — An object that has the capability of drying (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS1066939451>_). Properties: id, designMassFlowRate, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower, designVolumeFlowRate
ConvectionDryer — A Dryer that dries a material by bringing it in contact with a drying gas. Properties: id, airConsumption
HeatedSurfaceDryer — A Dryer that dries a material by radiation and/or conduction caused by a heated surface (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS2228449>_). Properties: id, heatedSurfaceArea
Separator — Properties: id, designVolumeFlowRate, efficiency, upperLimitAllowableDesignPressureDrop
ElectricalSeparator — A separator that uses electromagnetic, magnetic or electrostatic forces to separate phases. Properties: id, designPower

GravitationalSeparator — A fluid separator that is based on the difference in specific gravity for the substances to be separated (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS16042131>_). Properties: id, designPower, designRotationalSpeed
MechanicalSeparator — A fluid separator in which mechanical separation of fluids take place (from <http://data.posccaesar.org/rdl/RDS279134>_). Properties: id, designPower
ScrubbingSeparator — A separator that is intended to clean gas by washing the gas flow with water or with another liquid entering at the top of the vessel. Properties: id
CoolingTower — Properties: id, designHeatFlowRate, designVolumeFlowRate
CoolingTowerRotor — A rotor of a cooling tower. Properties: id, diameter, materialOfConstructionCode

DryCoolingTower — A CoolingTower that is an indirect contact heat exchanger where, by full utilization of dry surface coil sections, no direct contact (and no evaporation) occurs between air and water; hence the water is cooled totally by sensible heat transfer (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS14072386>_). Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower
SprayCooler — A CoolingTower that is based on spraying a coolant on a heated surface to be cooled. Properties: id, designSprayFlowRate

WetCoolingTower — A CoolingTower that derives its primary cooling effect from the evaporation that takes place when air and water are brought into direct contact. Properties: id, designRotationalSpeed, designShaftPower, designSprayFlowRate
SieveElement — A screening unit that is a component of a sieve. Properties: id, screeningArea, efficiency, materialOfConstructionCode, stageIdentifier, upperLimitPermeableParticleDiameter
Sieve — A device that removes particles from a fluid when the fluid passes through or separates particles or molecules according to their size. Properties: id, designMassFlowRate
RevolvingSieve — A revolving sieve that intends to sift out finer from coarser parts. Properties: id, designRotationalFrequency, designShaftPower
StationarySieve — A Sieve consisting of rakes or sieves, that, during operation, remains in a fixed position (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS2226669>_). Properties: id
VibratingSieve — A Sieve where the product to be sieved is transported over the mesh by vibration of the latter (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS2226670>_). Properties: id, designPower
Weigher — A functional object that is capable of weighing. Properties: id, designMassFlowRate, designPower
BatchWeigher — A Weigher that is operating in batch mode. Properties: id, designCapacityWeighingQuantities, upperLimitDesignLoad
ContinuousWeigher — A Weigher that weighs a mass flow rate in continuous mode. Properties: id, beltWidth
Motor — A driver that is powered by electricity or internal combustion (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS7191198>_). Properties: id, nominalPower, nominalRotationalFrequency
AlternatingCurrentMotor — Properties: id, alternatingCurrentFrequency, nominalVoltage
CombustionEngine — Properties: id, fuelType
DirectCurrentMotor — Properties: id, nominalVoltage

MotorAsComponent — A driver that is powered by electricity or internal combustion and is used as component of an apparatus or of a machine. Properties: id, nominalPower, nominalRotationalFrequency, subTagName

AlternatingCurrentMotorAsComponent — An electric motor driven by alternating electric current that is used as a component of an apparatus or of a machine. Properties: id, alternatingCurrentFrequency, nominalVoltage
CombustionEngineAsComponent — An engine intended to deliver power by means of burning fuels that is used as component of an apparatus or of a machine. Properties: id, fuelType
DirectCurrentMotorAsComponent — An electric motor for operation by direct current that is used as component of an apparatus or of a machine. Properties: id, nominalVoltage
ElectricGenerator — Properties: id, designOutletVoltage, designInletPower, designInletRotationalFrequency, designOutletPower
AlternatingCurrentGenerator — Properties: id, alternatingCurrentFrequency
DirectCurrentGenerator — An ElectricGenerator and current generator for the production of direct current (DC). Properties: id

Turbine — An object that is a rotary mechanical device that extracts energy from a fluid flow and converts it into useful work (from <http://data.15926.org/rdl/RDS313289>_). Properties: id, designRotationalFrequency, designPower
GasTurbine — A machine that is a rotary mechanical device extracting energy from a gas flow and converting it into useful work. Properties: id, fuelType
SteamTurbine — Properties: id, designInletMassFlow, designInletVolumeFlow
Vent — An object that has the capability of venting by being or having an opening that allows air, smoke, or gas to enter or leave a closed space to relief pressure and prevent vacuum. Properties: id
EquipmentVent — A Vent that is intended to release the pressure in a casing or to prevent airlocks in a fluid, and also acts as valve to release air trapped in the casing. Properties: id
PortNodePosition — Properties: id

Composition — This data item is an array of numbers that describe the chemical composition of a material. The order of items in the array is determined by the list of chemical components (ListOfMaterialComponents) in the corresponding MaterialTemplate object (see MaterialTemplate.ListOfComponents). Note: ISO 15926 uses the concept of CONCENTRATION and does not model the concept of material composition as an attribute. Properties: id, display

InformationVariant — This data structure is embedded in the InformationFlow object and can be configured to represent scalars and arrays of boolean, integer and real variables. Properties: id, booleanValue, doubleValue, integerValue, variantType, vectorSize
InstrumentationActivity — This is the base type for control and instrumentation functions that are specified as part of the process design. Properties: id, description, identifier, label

CalculatingProcessVariable — This InstrumentationActivity calculates an output that is some mathematical function of the inputs. This is a parent type for specialized calculations with specific purposes. Properties: id

CalculatingRatio — This CalculatingProcessVariable process calculates an output signal that is the ratio of the two input signals. It can be used to specify and design ratio control functions. If the two input signals are Dividend and Divisor, then OutputValue = Gain * Dividend/Divisor + Offset . Properties: id

CalculatingSplitRange — This CalculatingProcessVariable process calculates two output signals so that a single input signal can be used to manipulate two control elements using a split range. It can be used to specify and design split range control functions. Properties: id

SelectingProcessVariable — This InstrumentationActivity selects a single input signal to be sent to the output signal. It can be used to model high select and low select functions. Properties: id, selectorType

TransformingProcessVariable — This process performs a specified mathematical transformation on one or more input variables to calculate one or more output variables. The input and output variables are InformationPort objects owned by the type. Properties: id

ControllingProcessVariable — This InstrumentationActivity represents a process control activity. A block of this type calculates the value of a manipulated variable so that a measured variable is held at a specified set point. The set point can be supplied as an external InformationFlow. Properties: id

ConveyingSignal — This process transmits a signal between two processes. In practices, this process is only used if there will be a need to invest in specialized equipment and facilities, or if the properties of the signal are different at the input and output of the process. Most signal connections are represented by InformationFlow objects between InformationPort instances. Properties: id

MeasuringProcessVariable — This InstrumentationActivity measures a process variable and supplies its value at an outlet InformationPort. The measured variable is identified by reference to a parameter in any process step or port. Properties: id, measuredVariable

InstrumentationSystemActivity — An InstrumentationSystemActivity is a collection of related InstrumentationActivity instances that together perform a specified function. Thus a MeasuringProcessVariable and a ControllingProcessVariable activity can be grouped into a single InstrumentationSystemActivity that represents the control loop. Properties: id, description, identifier, label

ListOfMaterialComponents — This is an ordered list of PureMaterialComponent and CustomMaterialComponent objects. This is used in the MaterialTemplate to determine the structure of composition vectors in the Stream and MaterialStateType objects. Properties: id
MaterialComponent — This is the base type to chemical components in the model. It is parent class for PureMaterialComponent and CustomMaterialComponent. Properties: id, description, identifier, label

CustomMaterialComponent — A CustomMaterialComponent defines a custom chemical compound used to specify the chemical composition of a material. These compounds are usually pseudocomponents that are used to simulate the thermodynamic properties of complex mixtures of organic compounds with high molecular weight. Properties: id, projectReference

PureMaterialComponent — A PureMaterialComponent represents a MaterialComponent that is modelled as a pure chemical compound with defined composition and structure. This is used in the MaterialTemplate to document the composition vector and define properties for use in the process. Properties: id, chEBIIdentifier, iUPACIdentifier

MaterialState — This data structure contains the properties for a Stream. It contains one or more MaterialState objects: one for the total properties and then one for each of the phases present. Properties: id, description, identifier, label

MaterialStateType — This data structure represents the properties of a material or a single material phase. The MaterialState data structure for a Stream is built up of one or more of these data structures: one for the total properties and then one for each of the phases present. Properties: id, description, identifier, label

MaterialTemplate — This data structure defines the structure of Stream objects that correspond to a specific type of material. This structure contains information about the thermodynamic model used to represent this type of material. It contains the ListOfMaterialComponents: pure and pseudo components used to represent the system. It also determines the legend for a stream table when the model is used to represent a Process Flow Diagram. Properties: id, description, identifier, label, numberOfMaterialComponents, numberOfPhases, phaseLabel

Port — A port represents a transfer of material, energy or information into or out of a process step. It provides the anchor point for connecting two process steps to each other. The term is derived from SysML and IDEF0 representations of processes. Note that a port in DEXPI Process is a conceptual object. It represents a contract regarding the material, energy or information coming into or out of a process step. Properties: id, description, nominalDirection, identifier

EnergyPort — A Port that models the transfer of energy, of whatever form, into our out of a ProcessStep object. This type is parent to specific port types that specify the form of energy exchanged. This type can be used to represent energy requirements where the type of energy is unspecified. In practice, this type is abstract, and the child types are used in modelling. Properties: id

ElectricalEnergyPort — An EnergyPort that models the exchange of electrical energy between ProcessStep objects. The form of electrical energy exchanged is defined by the values of the properties of the ElectricalEnergyFlow into or out of the port. Roles referenced via PerformedRoles should have one of the following Names: - Instrumentation - Power - Utility Properties: id

MechanicalEnergyPort — A Port that models the transfer of mechanical energy into or out of a ProcessStep object. Roles referenced via PerformedRoles should have one of the following Names: - Input - Output Properties: id
ThermalEnergyPort — This is a Port that exchanges heat or thermal energy between processes. Roles referenced via PerformedRoles should have one of the following Names: - Input - Output Properties: id

InformationPort — A Port that models the transfer of information, of whatever form, into or out of a ProcessStep object. This type is used to represent control signals. Roles referenced via PerformedRoles should have one of the following Names: - Feedback - Input - Output - Override - Setpoint Properties: id

MaterialPort — A Port that models the transfer of material, of whatever form, into or out of a ProcessStep object. This type is used for flow of material: solids, liquids and gases. Roles referenced via PerformedRoles should have one of the following Names: - Air - BottomProduct - ChemicalFeed - Discharge - Drain - Exhaust - Feed - Fuel - HeavyLiquid - Inlet - LeanSolvent - LightLiquid - Liquid - LiquidInlet - LiquidOutlet - Outlet - Product - Reboil - Reflux - Relief - RichSolvent - Sidedraw - Suction - TopProduct - Vapour - VapourInlet - VapourOutlet - Vent - Waste Properties: id
ProcessConnection — This data structure is the abstract parent for all connections between blocks in the DEXPI Process model. Properties: id, description, identifier, label

EnergyFlow — A ProcessConnection that defines the flow of energy between two instances of EnergyPort. This is used to model flows of energy where the form of energy is unspecified. This type usually abstract and child types of this type are used to model energy flows with a specified form of energy. Properties: id

ElectricalEnergyFlow — A ProcessConnection that defines the flow of energy between two instances of ElectricalEnergyPort. This is used to model flows of electricity into out of the port. The form of electrical energy is defined by the properties of the object. Properties: id
MechanicalEnergyFlow — A ProcessConnection that defines the flow of mechanical energy two instances of MechanicalEnergyPort. Properties: id
ThermalEnergyFlow — This data structure defines the properties of a flow of heat or thermal energy between two ThermalEnergyPort objects. Properties: id

InformationFlow — A ProcessConnection that defines the flow of information between two instances of InformationPort. This is used to model signals and other information flows into out of the port. Properties: id
ProcessStep — The ProcessStep type is the parent type for all process steps in the model. Properties: id, description, identifier, label, hierarchyLevel

Emitting — This type represents the destination for a flow out of a process that can be regarded as an emission to the environment. It can be used instead of a Sink. It is provided as a convenience for calculating emissions and sustainability calculations. Properties: id
ExchangingThermalEnergy — This process transfers thermal energy between two or more streams of material. This process is realized by a heat exchanger. Properties: id, method
Flaring — This SupplyingThermalEnergy process represents the flare system in a process plant. Properties: id

FormingSolidMaterial — This process takes a material containing solids and forms the solid material into particles with specified sizes and shape. It is the parent type for Pelletizing and Extruding. Properties: id
Extruding — This FormingSolidMaterial process takes solid material and forms it by forcing it through a specially designed opening, so that the material is given a specific shape. Properties: id
Pelletizing — This FormingSolidMaterial process takes solid material and forms it into, pellets, small particles of uniform size and shape. Properties: id
GeneratingFlow — This is a base type for processes with the purpose of generating flow and/or increasing pressure of a fluid stream. The child types are Pumping and Compressing. Properties: id

Coalescing — This is an IncreasingParticleSize process in which small droplets of a liquid phase are made to coalesce into larger droplets, which can then be separated from the mixture. Properties: id

Compressing — This GeneratingFlow process represents compression of gases to increase pressure and generate a flow of gas. The physical principle used to compress the gas can be specified by selecting a value from the CompressionMethod enumeration. Properties: id, method

Pumping — This GeneratingFlow process represents transfer of mechanical energy to a liquid to increase pressure and generate a flow. The physical principle used to compress the gas can be specified by selecting a value from the PumpingMethod enumeration. Properties: id, method
IncreasingParticleSize — This process takes a material containing solids and performs an operation so that the solids have a larger particle size. Properties: id

Agglomerating — A solids-processing process for IncreasingParticleSize in which particles bind together and coalesce into larger particles, held together by relatively weak forces. See also Flocculating and Pelletizing. Note that Pelletizing is a subtype of FormingSolidMaterial. Properties: id
Crystallizing — This IncreasingParticleSize process is based on the formation of crystals from a feed fluid. This then allows the separation of the resulting solids from the liquid. Properties: id
Flocculating — This IncreasingParticleSize process produces larger particles, flocs, through aggregation and coalesence under the influence addition of surfactant chemicals. Properties: id
Mixing — This is the base class for processes that combine several flows of material into a single flow. Properties: id
Humidifying — This Mixing process increases the water or liquid content of a material stream by mixing a feed with the water or liquid. Properties: id
Kneading — This Mixing process produces a solid material as a uniform mass by mechanically folding, pressing and stretching of the material. Properties: id

MixingSimple — This is a Mixing process that simply combines one or more inlet flows into an outlet flow. This process step is used to represent converging branches of flows in a PFD or BFD. It is the counterpart of Splitting. Properties: id
RotaryMixing — This Mixing process uses an externally powered rotating impeller to produce a homogeneous material. Properties: id

StaticMixing — This Mixing process uses a stationary element in the flow of material to produce the necessary homogeneity in the material that comes out of the process. It is realized by a StaticMixer. Properties: id
Packaging — This process takes a flow of material and processes it into packages that allow transport and distribution. Properties: id
ReactingChemicals — This process performs chemical reactions on material in order to produce products of value or to remove undesirable chemical compounds. Properties: id, method
ReducingParticleSize — A process where a solid material is broken down into particles with a smaller size. This is the parent class for Cutting, Milling, Crushing and Grinding. Properties: id
Crushing — This ReducingParticleSize process takes solid material and breaks it into smaller pieces by an externally applied mechanical force. See also Grinding and Milling. Properties: id
Cutting — This ReducingParticleSize process separates solid material into smaller parts using an edged implement or knife. Properties: id
Grinding — This ReducingParticleSize process produces fine particles by abrasion of solid material. Properties: id
Milling — This ReducingParticleSize process divides solid material into smaller particles with precise sizes and shapes. Properties: id
RemovingThermalEnergy — This process removes enthalpy from a material in order to reduce temperature or change the state of the material. See also Cooling. Properties: id, method

Cooling — This RemovingThermalEnergy process has the purpose of reducing the enthalpy content of a material through heat exchange with the environment or a cooling medium. See also ExchangingThermalEnergy, which can be used to model the same process in cases where the cooling medium system is defined. Properties: id

Separating — This is the base type for all processes where one or more feeds are transformed into streams of material, each with different intensive properties and chemical composition. Properties: id

SeparatingByElectromagneticForce — This is a Separating process where a material mixture is separated by the application of an electrical or magnetic field. This type is parent to SeparatingByElectrostaticForce and SeparatingByMagneticForce. Properties: id
SeparatingByElectrostaticForce — This is a SeparatingByElectromagneticForce process where a material mixture is separated by the application of an electrostatic field. Properties: id
SeparatingByMagneticForce — This is a SeparatingByElectromagneticForce process where a material mixture is separated by the application of a magnetic field. Properties: id

SeparatingByFlash — This is a SeparatingByThermalProcess process where a fluid mixture is separated into a vapour phase and a liquid phase in a vessel, usually after a sudden decrease in pressure. This is a single-stage process, unlike Distilling. Properties: id
SeparatingByPhaseSeparation — This is a Separating process where the materials form distinct phases, which can then be separated. Properties: id

SeparatingByCentrifugalForce — This is a SeparatingByPhaseSeparation process where a fluid mixture is separated into a heavy phase and light phase through the external application of mechanical energy to produce centrifugal forces. Properties: id

SeparatingByCyclonicMotion — This is a SeparatingByPhaseSeparation process where a fluid mixture is separated into a heavy phase and light phase through the centrifugal forces generated by the flow of fluids through a cyclone arrangement. Properties: id
SeparatingByGravity — This SeparatingByPhaseSeparation process separates substances based on the influence of gravity on substances with different density or specific gravity. Properties: id

SeparatingByPhysicalProcess — This Separating process uses a physical phenomenon, such as mass transfer, ion exchange or surface tension to separate materials. Its child types are SeparatingByContact, SeparatingByIonExchange, Absorbing, Adsorbing and SeparatingBySurfaceTension. Properties: id

Absorbing — A subtype of SeparatingByPhysicalProcess where separation is based on mass transfer of material from a gas to a liquid. This type is also used to represent desorbing, where the mass transfer is from the liquid to the gas. Properties: id

Adsorbing — A subtype of SeparatingByPhysicalProcess where separation is based on mass transfer of material from a fluid to the surface of a solid. This type is also used to represent the reverse process, where the mass transfer is from the surface to the fluid. Properties: id
SeparatingByContact — This is a SeparatingByPhysicalProcess process where materials are brought into contact with each to transfer mass and energy. Properties: id

SeparatingByIonExchange — This SeparatingByPhysicalProcess is a reversible interchange of one kind of ion present on an insoluble solid with another of like charge present in a solution surrounding the solid with the reaction being used especially for softening or demineralizing water, the purification of chemicals, or the separation of substances. Properties: id

SeparatingBySurfaceTension — This is a Separating process where the materials are separated through a difference in surface forces between different liquid phases or between liquids and solid particles. Froth flotation is a typical process of this type. Properties: id
SeparatingByThermalProcess — This is a Separating process where the materials are separated through the application of heat or thermal energy. Properties: id

Distilling — This SeparatingByThermalProcess process uses boiling, condensing and countercurrent contacting of liquid and vapour to separate chemical components with a difference in relative volatility. Properties: id

StabilizingDistilling — This Distilling process has the purpose of producing a stabilized liquid product by removing the volatile chemical compounds that would otherwise make the product unstable for transport or storage. Properties: id
StrippingDistilling — This Distilling process has the purpose of removing volatile components from a fluid. Properties: id
VacuumDistilling — This is a Distilling process that is conducted at sub-atmospheric pressures. Properties: id
Drying — This SeparatingByThermalProcess process removes moisture or liquids from a solid material, producing a solid product with a lower content of the liquid components. Properties: id

Evaporating — This SeparatingByThermalProcess process applies thermal energy to drive off moisture or other volatile liquid as gas. This results in a vapour product and a more concentrated liquid or solid product. Properties: id
SeparatingMechanically — This is a parent process where the materials are separated by a mechanical operation, such as Filtering, Skimming or Sieving. Properties: id
Filtering — This SeparatingMechanically process separates solids from fluids by passing the fluid through a porous barrier. Properties: id

Sieving — This SeparatingMechanically processs for solids is based on particle size. Material is passed over a series of screens with a specified aperture size. Smaller particles pass through the screens, while larger particles remain on the screen. Properties: id

Skimming — This is a SeparatingMechanically process in which a lighter immiscible fluid, such as oil, is separated from a heaver fluid, such as water, by mechanical wiping of the surface of the heavier fluid. Properties: id
Sink — This type is used to represent a flow of material out of the process. It can be used to represent an outgoing off-page connector in a PFD or BFD. Properties: id, sourceReference
Source — This type is used to represent a flow of material into the process. It can be used to represent an incoming off-page connector in a PFD or BFD. Properties: id, sinkReference

Splitting — This type is used to represent the splitting of a material or energy flow. This type is abstract, and the child types SplittingMaterial and SplittingEnergy are used in practice. Properties: id

SplittingEnergy — This type is used to represent the splitting of an energy flow. The intensive properties of the flow remain the same, but the total amount of flow (power) is divided among the outlet ports. Properties: id
SplittingMaterial — This process splits an incoming flow of material into two or more outgoing flows of material. The intensive properties of the material flows remain the same. Properties: id

SteeringFlow — The base type for processes that manipulate the rate of flow of material into and out of the process step. This process is usually realized using a valve. Child types of this type have been specified to support design of the process control and safety systems. Properties: id

BlowingDown — This SteeringFlow process is used to depressurise or blow down a process, removing the contents of a process rapidly and safely to prevent unsafe conditions or shut down the process. This process is usually realized as a set of blow-down or depressurisation valves. Properties: id
Draining — This supporting SteeringFlow process is used to manage leakages and handle the emptying of a plant for maintenance. Properties: id
FeedingMaterial — This SteeringFlow process supplies material to a process at a controllable rate. This process can be used to represent solid feeding processes or dosing systems. Properties: id
LimitingFlow — This SteeringFlow process is used to ensure that the flow of material remains below a specified value. This process is usually realized using a flow orifice. Properties: id

PreventingBackflow — This SteeringFlow process is used to ensure that a flow of material cannot be reversed. This process is used in safety design and is realized by a check valve or non-return valve. Properties: id
RegulatingFlow — A SteeringFlow process where a flow of material is manipulated over a continuous range of values. The desired flow rate is supplied in the XG1 InformationPort. Properties: id
RelievingOverpressure — A SteeringFlow process where a flow of material is manipulated to ensure that the pressure in a system shall not exceed a specified value. Properties: id
RelievingVacuum — A SteeringFlow process where a flow of material is manipulated to ensure that the pressure in a system shall not become sub-atmospheric. Properties: id

RelievingVacuumAndOverpressure — A SteeringFlow process where a flow of material is manipulated to ensure that the pressure in a system shall neither become sub-atmospheric nor exceed a specified value. Properties: id
ShuttingOffFlow — This is a SteeringFlow process with the purpose of shutting off flow for operational and/or safety reasons. It is usually realized by an on-off valve. Properties: id

StoringMaterial — An abstract process step that is the parent class for processes that accumulate material. It is often the intention of these steps that the accumulated material can be used as supply for other process steps. Properties: id

StoringFluids — This StoringMaterial process accumulates fluids: gases and liquids. It can be connected to a filling flow of material and an optional emptying flow of material. In this way it can be used as supplier of material for other process steps. The principle and construction of the storage is unspecified. The sub-types of this type are differentiated according to whether the storage is pressurised or not. StoringInTank is used for atmospheric storage of liquids, whereas StoringInPressureVessel is used for storage of gases and fluids at above-atmospheric or sub-atmospheric pressure. Properties: id

StoringInPressureVessel — This StoringFluids process accumulates fluid materials in a PressureVessel. This process assumes atmospheric storage of the material at pressures above or below atmospheric pressure. Use StoringInTank where fluid is stored at atmospheric conditions. It can be connected to a filling flow of material and an optional emptying flow of material. In this way it can be used as supplier of material for other process steps. Properties: id

StoringInTank — This StoringFluids process accumulates fluid, solid or mixed materials in a Tank. This process assumes atmospheric storage of the material. Use StoringInPressureVessel where fluid or gas is to be stored at above-atmospheric or sub-atmospheric conditions. It can be connected to a filling flow of material and an optional emptying flow of material. In this way it can be used as supplier of material for other process steps. Properties: id

StoringSolids — This StoringMaterial process accumulates solid material. It can be connected to a filling flow of material and an optional emptying flow of material. In this way it can be used as supplier of material for other process steps. The principle and construction of the storage is unspecified. Properties: id
StoringInSilo — This StoringSolids process is realized by a Silo. Properties: id
StoringEnergy — An abstract process step that is the parent class for processes that store energy. Properties: id

StoringElectricalEnergy — This process step stores electrical energy. It can be connected to a charging flow of electricity and can also be used as a supplier of electrical energy to other process steps. The principle of storage is unspecified. The StoringInBattery type can be used when a chemical battery is used as the storage system. Properties: id

StoringInBattery — This StoringElectricalEnergy process step stores electrical energy in a battery. It can be connected to a charging flow of electricity and can also be used as a supplier of electrical energy to other process steps. Properties: id
StoringMechanicalEnergy — This process accumulates and stores mechanical energy. Properties: id
StoringThermalEnergy — This process accumulates and stores thermal energy for use in other processes. A calorifier is an example of this process in HVAC systems. Properties: id
SupplyingEnergy — This process is a source of energy for use in other processes. Properties: id
SupplyingMaterial — This process is a source of material for use in other processes. Properties: id
SupplyingFluids — This process is a source of fluid materials (liquids, gases or multiphase mixtures) for use in other processes. Properties: id
SupplyingElectricalEnergy — This process is a source of electrical energy for use in other processes. Properties: id
GeneratingACPower — This SupplyingElectricalEnergy process produces alternating current electrical energy from mechanical energy. Properties: id
GeneratingDCPower — This SupplyingElectricalEnergy process produces alternating current electrical energy from mechanical energy. Properties: id
GeneratingInFuelCell — This process generates electricity using a fuel cell. Properties: id

SupplyingMechanicalEnergy — This process is a source of mechanical energy for use in other processes. It is the parent type for the DrivingByEngine, DrivingByMotor and DrivingByTurbine types. Properties: id
DrivingByEngine — This SupplyingMechanicalEnergy process uses an internal combustion engine as its source of energy. Properties: id, method
DrivingByMotor — This SupplyingMechanicalEnergy process uses an electric motor as its source of energy. Properties: id, method
DrivingByTurbine — This SupplyingMechanicalEnergy process uses an turbine as its source of energy. Properties: id, method
SupplyingSolids — This process is a source of solid material for use in other processes. Properties: id
SupplyingThermalEnergy — This process is a source of thermal energy for use in other processes. Properties: id, method

Boiling — This SupplyingThermalEnergy process vaporises a fluid. This process can be realized as a boiler, heat exchanger or fired heater. The process can also be used to represent the re-boiling subprocess in a distillation process. Properties: id
GeneratingSteam — This process produces steam for use in other processes. Properties: id
HeatingElectrical — This SupplyingThermalEnergy process increases the enthalpy content of one or more material streams through the application of electrical energy. Properties: id
HeatingInFurnace — This SupplyingThermalEnergy process increases the enthalpy content of one or more material streams by passing them through a fired heater or furnace. Properties: id
TransportingEnergy — This process transmits energy between processes. Properties: id
TransportingElectricalEnergy — This process transmits electrical energy between processes. Properties: id
TransportingMechanicalEnergy — This TransportingEnergy process transmits mechanical energy (including rotational energy) between processes. This can be realized by a shaft. Properties: id

TransportingThermalEnergy — This TransportingEnergy process transmits thermal energy (including heat) between processes. This is different to a heat exchanging process step in the sense that the transporting thermal energy process step intends to preserve the transported energy between input and output. Properties: id
TransportingMaterial — This process moves material between processes. Child types detail the kind of the transported material (fluid vs. solid). Properties: id

TransportingFluids — This process moves fluids: gas, liquid or multiphase flows, between processes. It is also used to model distribution processes, such as steam supply systems, gas reticulation networks, cooling water systems and flare systems. Three child types are used to specify the realisation of this process, as the realization has implications for process design. The child types are TransportingFluidsInChannel, TransportingFluidsInHose and TransportingFluidsInPipe. Properties: id
TransportingFluidsInChannel — This TransportingFluids process is realized by an open channel or drain. This type can be used to model open drain systems. Properties: id
TransportingFluidsInHose — This TransportingFluids process is realized by a flexible connector or hose. This type can be used to model hose or flexible piping systems. Properties: id

TransportingFluidsInPipe — This TransportingFluids process is realized by a rigid connector, duct or pipe. This type can be used to pipeline systems, piping-based fluid distribution systems and ducting systems. Properties: id

TransportingSolids — This process moves solid material between processes. Two child types are used to specify the realisation of this process, as the realization has implications for process design. The child types are TransportingSolidsContinuously and TransportingSolidsDiscontinuously. Properties: id
TransportingSolidsContinuously — This process moves solid material between processes using a continuous operation, such as a conveyor of various types. Properties: id
TransportingSolidsDiscontinuously — This process moves solid material between processes using a discontinuous or batch operation, such as a vehicle, container or crane. Properties: id
ProcessStepDetail — This type is the parent type for processes that cannot be run independently of another process. Properties: id, description, identifier, label
Agitating — This ProcessStepDetail provides shear forces to liquids in another process, with the purpose of mixing, increasing heat transfer rates or increasing mass transfer rates. Properties: id

ContactingInPacking — This ProcessStepDetail is used to represent a process carried out in a packed bed. Its role is to represent packing shown in process flow diagrams and to support the functional breakdown of complex processing systems. See also ContactingOnTray. Properties: id

ContactingOnTray — This ProcessStepDetail is used to represent a process carried out in an assembly of trays. Its role is to represent trays shown in process flow diagrams and to support the functional breakdown of complex processing systems. See also ContactingInPacking. Roles referenced via PerformedRoles should have one of the following Names: - Bottom - Feed - Monitored - Top Properties: id, number

SupplyingThermalEnergyWithBurner — This ProcessStepDetail is used to specify a combustion process as a sub-process of some other process, such as a sub-type of SupplyingThermalEnergy. This process is usually realized by one or more Burner components. Properties: id
Stream — This data structure defines the properties of a flow of fluid or solid material between two MaterialPort objects. Properties: id
ProcessModel — Properties: id
